title: the canon-commit gate blocks the commit and its own remedy cannot unblock it, because st attach does not write the extract the way the remedy says it does
body:
**`canon_commit_check.sh` BLOCKS THE COMMIT AND ITS REMEDY DOES NOT UNBLOCK IT.** Following the remedy exactly leaves the operator refused forever, because the step it names does not do the thing it says it does.

=== THE REMEDY, VERBATIM FROM THE BLOCKING GATE ===

    THE ORDER MATTERS AND THE OBVIOUS ONE DOES NOT WORK. `intent st attach <ST> <rel-path>
    --from <file>` FIRST -- that is the ONLY writer of an attachment, and it updates the
    store AND the extract in one step.

**The clause `and it updates the store AND the extract in one step` is false.** Driven on `ST0056/impl.md`, 2026-08-31:

    disk BEFORE attach:  1126 bytes, mtime 13:29:48
    intent st attach ST0056 impl.md --from <5327-byte file>   ->  ok: impl.md written to ST0056
    disk AFTER  attach:  1126 bytes, mtime 13:29:48

The store took the 5327 bytes. The extract was not written, not even touched -- the mtime is unchanged, and it dates from 2026-08-14. Re-running `attach` a second time changed nothing, so this is the verb's behaviour and not a first-run condition.

=== AND THE ESTATE CONTAINS BOTH REMEDIES, WHICH CONTRADICT EACH OTHER ===

`intent doctor` names the same drift and gives the OPPOSITE instruction, and doctor's is the one that matches the measured behaviour:

    residue: intent/st/ST0056/impl.md -- attachment-drift -- ...
    remedy: ... put the text you meant where you want it BY HAND: an attachment is
    AUTHORED, so no sync direction rewrites it for you

So one tool says a verb will write the extract for you, and another says nothing will and you must do it by hand. **An operator who trusts the blocking gate loops; an operator who trusts `doctor` gets through.** The gate is the one that stops work, so it is the one whose text is load-bearing.

=== WHAT THE FIX IS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT ===

The fix is to the gate's REMEDY TEXT, not to `st attach`. Whether an attachment SHOULD have a canon-to-disk writer is `0082`'s subject and is not reopened here -- `0082` already establishes the mechanism in its own words (*attachments flow disk -> canon only ... and there is no canon -> disk writer*), and it is filed as high.

**This is a separate defect from `0082` and is filed separately for that reason:** `0082` is about `sync --to-disk` reporting success while skipping an attachment; this is about a GATE instructing the operator to perform a step that cannot achieve what the gate requires. Different file, different fix, and this one blocks commits.

The working sequence, for whoever repairs the text: `intent st attach <ST> <path> --from <file>` to write the store, then write the same bytes to the extract path BY HAND (from canon, so the SSOT is the source), then stage and commit canon and the file together. That is what was done here and the gate passed.

=== WHY IT SURVIVED ===

The remedy is prose inside a guard. Nothing drives it. Every other claim this gate makes is checked against the artefact it names; its instructions to the human are the one part of it that no instrument reads, which is the same shape as an `as-observed` register row that nothing compares to behaviour (`0198`).
